mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic context.
failure_condition: Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day SPX returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or average 20-day returns in lowest 20% FEDFUNDS observations are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 6.0%, it signals labor market weakness that depresses consumer spending and corporate earnings, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >55% of observations when UNRATE > 6.0% (10-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages signal robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Interaction effect between HOUST and RSAFS is insignificant (p>0.05) in 20-day return regression, or average returns when both series exceed 12mo MA are not positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During supply contraction regimes (INDPRO growth < 0%), declining industrial production signals reduced economic output that lowers corporate profitability, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >55% of periods when INDPRO growth < 0% (10-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1000.0, it indicates a weakening housing market that reduces consumer wealth and spending, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >55% of observations when HOUST < 1000.0 (10-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising > 0.25pp in 3 months), higher interest rates increase equity discount rates and reduce corporate borrowing, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >55% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25pp in 3 months (10-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: Higher non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicate a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days regardless of economic context.
failure_condition: Rank IC between PAYEMS and 5-day SPX returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or average 5-day returns in highest 20% PAYEMS observations are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in industrial production (INDPRO) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages signal synchronized economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Interaction effect between INDPRO and RSAFS is insignificant (p>0.05) in 60-day return regression, or average returns when both series exceed 12mo MA are not positive (t-test p>0.05).
